newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: New private Irish utilities company set up.
newsitem.headline: New private Irish utilities company set up.

text.p: National Utilities, a company which will develop opportunities in the public utilities sector, has been set up by three leading businessmen.

Denis O'Brien, chairman of Esat Telecom, management consultant Leslie Buckley and John O'Connor, who has worked at director level with British Aerospace, Siemens Plessey and Thorn EMI Electronics, are behind the move, a statement from National Utilities said.
The company is at an advanced stage of discussion with internationally-renowned utilities companies with a view to establishing joint venture projects in the Irish market.
National Utilities will initially concentrate on power generation and waste water management projects where a number of forces, including EU directives, are driving the pace of change.

It has been tracking the liberalisation of the power generation business which will see 32 percent of that market become available for private involvement under an EU directive adopted by the European Council of Ministers in December.

National Utilities said it would become involved in specific power generation projects and will also investigate opportunities for involvement in the construction of alternative energy-driven power generation facilities.

In the water sector, where such a high level of Ireland's waste water discharges do not meet European standards, the company has been examining opportunities for co-operation between the private and public sectors in the creation of advanced treatement facilities, it said.
